impacted.role: applyFiltersClientSide (line 1454) filters both local and remote mode with priority equality; the 0/1/2/3/a/R key handlers (lines 658-723) set m.priority; newModel (line 130) sets the defaults every launch
buildViewStateString (line 14) renders 'Priority: MEDIUM' etc. and 'Hidden: N'
getDefaultDBPath (line 318) is the existing XDG path pattern (env var, else the default under the home directory)

constraints.text: Local mode fetches all content and filters client-side too (the local branch of fetchItemsWithState says 'unified with remote mode'), so one function decides the visible set in both modes.

0 sets priority 'unprioritized' and shows only items with no priority; 'a' sets priority 'all' and hides unprioritized items with a 'Hidden: N' count; no other key toggles unprioritized visibility, so #52's standalone toggle no longer exists.

Measured on cerebro 2026-10-07: 21,095 unread unprioritized items against 6,668 unread prioritized ones, and 6 of the operator's 24 upvotes are on unprioritized items (latest 2026-09-29), so the unprioritized-only view is in use for rescuing items the evaluator left out, and a floor below LOW would be 76% unscored items.
The TUI resolves XDG directories by reading the env var and falling back to the default under the home directory; it has no XDG_STATE_HOME use yet.
Principle II: a view file that could not be read must be distinguishable from a first launch with no file.
Under the floor model, 'a' (all prioritized) and 3 (LOW and above) select the same items, so one state can back both keys.

reuse.what: applyFiltersClientSide, the one filter both modes use
getDefaultDBPath's XDG resolution pattern, for the state directory
